newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine builder opens bond mkt for small firms.
newsitem.headline: Argentine builder opens bond mkt for small firms.

text.p: Construir SA, a provincial Argentine construction company, said Thursday it is launching a bond, thus leading the way in opening the market for alternative financing for smaller Argentine firms.

Construir became the first Argentine PYME (small and medium sized company) to issue a negotiable bond at the end of last year aimed at institutional investors. On Thursday it said at a presentation it is entering the market again with a three year $2.5 million bullet issue.
Jaime Garbarsky, President of Empresa Constructora Inmobiliaria del Plata SA, the guarantor of the issue, told Reuters "Construir is doing this to have a presence in the capital markets."
Although the issue is very small even by Argentine standards, Garbarsky said "this opens the way for alternative financing in Argentina for small firms to bank loans."

For decades extremely high interest rates have represented a major barrier to the growth of smaller Argentine companies because of high costs of credit compared with large local firms that have been able to raise capital more cheaply abroad. Garbarsky said "we want to show that the market can work for small firms as well."
Market rates have fallen dramatically in recent years, especially thanks to the Convertibility plan that has pegged the value of the peso to the dollar since 1991.
Construir's bond will be a dollar issue and carry a 14 percent coupon with interest payments payable every six months. It will be issue at 99.53.

The bond is aimed at "raising the working capital of the company." The company hopes to entice local pension funds, banks and insurance companies with the bond. Construir's last issue was a two year bond with a coupon of 15 percent.
